Knee Misfit and the Geometry of the Aperiodic Component

Publication figure built from real specparam fits on simulated spectra

Author

Daniel Borek

This notebook generates a three-panel publication figure. Every curve is a real specparam fit to a simulated power spectrum — nothing is drawn analytically by hand.

  • Panel A — Misfit. A spectrum with a genuine knee is fit with both the knee and the fixed aperiodic model. The fixed model has no plateau term, so it tilts a straight line through the data and underestimates the exponent. The exponent is routinely read as “the 1/f slope” — a biased exponent means a biased physiological interpretation.
  • Panel B — Knee parameter. Low vs. high knee (k), exponent held fixed. k sets the plateau height and the knee frequency f_k = k^(1/χ).
  • Panel C — Exponent. Low vs. high exponent (χ), knee held fixed. χ sets the high-frequency slope; the low-frequency plateau is shared.

All text is exported as vector paths (svg.fonttype='path'), so the SVGs embed identically in slides and the thesis regardless of installed fonts.

Panel A — Misfit: fixed mode flattens the exponent

The fixed model reaches an R² that looks perfectly acceptable, yet its exponent is biased low by tens of percent: with no plateau term it pivots a straight line through plateau and slope. Reading that exponent as a “1/f / E:I” index would carry the bias straight into the physiological claim.

Panel B — Knee parameter: plateau height and knee position

Panel C — Exponent: high-frequency slope

Export

Each panel is saved standalone (for individual slides); the combined figure is assembled by nesting those standalone SVGs side by side, so every panel keeps the exact layout shown above.
